description:
Digital Marketing Executive

North Bristol £33,000-£36,000 per annum Office-based, 5 days per week

We're looking for a hungry, proactive and commercially minded Digital Marketing Executive to join an established and successful independent business in Bristol.

The role is ultimately about driving more visitors, increasing sales and helping the business grow through effective, engaging marketing. You'll have the opportunity to take ownership of a broad mix of digital and traditional activity and see the direct impact of your work.

You'll be someone who is happy to research, teach yourself new skills and find solutions when you come across something you haven't done before. You'll have a solid grounding in marketing and digital, but we're open to someone whose experience is stronger in some areas than others and who is keen to develop.

We're looking for someone who is resourceful, self-motivated and confident working autonomously, who takes ownership, gets things done and understands that great marketing should deliver commercial results.

- Creating engaging social media and digital content
- Supporting SEO and paid digital activity
- Planning and delivering email marketing campaigns
- Supporting seasonal campaigns, promotions and events
- Using analytics and reporting to understand performance
- Helping to improve the customer journey and online experience
- Supporting traditional marketing activity including print, advertising and promotional materials
- Working with colleagues and external suppliers to deliver marketing activity

What We're Looking For

You'll ideally have experience or knowledge in some of the following:
- Digital marketing and social media
- Content creation
- SEO and website management
- E-commerce
- Email marketing
- Google Analytics and Google Search Console
- Google Ads
- Canva

You do not need to have experience in all of these areas. A strong marketing foundation, digital confidence and a willingness to learn are more important.

What's On Offer
- £33,000-£36,000 per annum, depending on experience
- A varied role with genuine ownership
- The opportunity to broaden and develop your digital marketing skills
- A supportive and collaborative working environment
- Generous holiday allowance
- A range of company benefits

If you're a self-motivated marketer who is curious, capable and keen to keep learning, we'd love to hear from you.

- Maintain high standards of confidentiality, information security and data protection.

- Assist with file audits and ensure documentation meets required standards.
- Ensure work is completed accurately and in accordance with relevant legal and regulatory requirements.

Business Development & CRM

- Input and manage client, referral and relationship data.
- Support colleagues in using the CRM effectively.

Teamwork & Continuous Improvement
- Build strong relationships across the Corporate team and wider organisation.
- Work collaboratively to ensure work is completed accurately and efficiently.
- Coordinate meetings, training and team activities where required.
- Take ownership of small projects and administrative initiatives.
- Contribute ideas to improve processes and operational efficiency.

About You
You will ideally have:
- Previous experience as a Legal Assistant, Legal Secretary, Legal PA, PA or similar support professional - essential.

- Strong organisational, administrative and prioritisation skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- A good understanding of client service and relationship management.

What We're Looking For

If you are an experienced Legal Assistant, Legal Secretary, Legal PA or professional services administrator looking for your next opportunity in Bristol, we would love to hear from you.

title: Service Coordinator - Mental Health
description:
We are looking for an experienced and compassionate leader to join our Mental Health Services as a Peripatetic Service Coordinator, supporting teams across Bristol and South Gloucestershire.

What does "Peripatetic" mean for this role?

In this position, "peripatetic" means you will provide cover across our different regional sites, rather than being based permanently at a single location. However, you will not be traveling to a different site every day. You will typically be assigned to one specific project or location for extended periods-often weeks or months at a time-to provide stable, ongoing support where it is needed most.

An exciting pathway to permanence:

Because you will become embedded within the teams you support, this role offers a genuine opportunity to move into a permanent Service Coordinator position should a suitable vacancy arise and align with your skills, experience and success in the role.

About the role

This is an exciting opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of people with complex mental health needs while leading and developing high-performing teams.

As a Service Coordinator, you will lead teams to deliver person-centred support that enables people to achieve their goals, build independence, and gain the skills and confidence to live fulfilling lives in their communities. You will support individuals to build resilience, develop practical life skills, strengthen community connections, and take greater control of their future.

You will be an inspiring and supportive leader with excellent communication and listening skills, able to motivate, develop, and empower colleagues to deliver outstanding support. A strong understanding of person-centred practice and a commitment to promoting positive mental health, wellbeing, and recovery-focused support are essential.

You will ensure services are delivered safely, effectively, and in line with relevant legislation, regulations, and organisational standards, while demonstrating positive outcomes for the people we support.

Travel & Vehicle Requirements

You must have access to your own reliable vehicle for business use. We fully understand that travel is a key part of this role, which is why all business mileage is reimbursed at our standard company rate.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the day-to-day operation of services, including rota planning and resource allocation, to ensure people receive the right support at the right time.
- Supporting teams to co-produce and regularly review support plans, risk assessments and positive risk management strategies.
- Providing regular supervision, coaching and performance support to team members, while ensuring training and development needs are met.
- Contributing to referrals, assessments and service transition planning.
- Monitoring service budgets and expenditure in line with organisational expectations.
- Providing direct, hands-on support when required and leading by example in delivering high-quality care and support.

About you

The successful candidate will:
- Demonstrate strong leadership skills, with experience of supervising, leading or coordinating a team.
- Be highly organised and able to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
- Have experience supporting people with complex mental health needs and a sound understanding of recovery-focused practice.
- Be confident in responding to people who are experiencing acute mental illness, in dynamic risk management and developing escalation plans to ensure that people receive the support that they need.
- Have knowledge of mental health services, legislation and best practice, including experience of trauma-informed approaches.
- Be flexible to work across a seven-day service, including a variety of shift patterns as required.

Why join us?

This is an excellent opportunity to work across a variety of services, develop talented teams and play a key role in shaping high-quality mental health support across Bristol and South Gloucestershire. You'll be joining an organisation that is committed to empowering people, investing in its workforce and continually improving the services it delivers.

At Milestones Trust we recognise that without the hard work, commitment and passion of our staff, we wouldn't be the charity that we are today. In return, we are committed to rewarding you with a competitive pay and benefits package including:
- 34 days' annual leave, including recognised public holidays
- Learning and development to support your career growth
- Nationally recognised qualifications, from entry level care to management
- Flexible working, with rotas provided in advance
- Occupational Sick Pay after two years, increasing with service
- Health Cash Plan after probation, offering at least £695 cashback for health treatments (dental, optical, therapies, maternity/paternity, prescriptions)
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Free enhanced DBS check
- Dayforce Wallet, giving you access to your earnings before payday
- Employee referral scheme with financial rewards
- Employee Assistance Programme from day one, offering confidential 24/7 support
- Company pension scheme to help grow your retirement savings

We pride ourselves with being able to offer staff opportunities to develop and progress their careers within the Trust.

This is a varied role within a busy hospital environment and would suit someone who is organised, reliable and enjoys working as part of a team. You will have regular contact with patients, including communicating with them by telephone, so you should be confident, professional and compassionate when speaking with patients and their families.

title: Reception and Appointment Clerk
description: The Reception and Appointment Clerk works across a number of sites providing reception, administrative and appointment booking support for Haematology and Oncology services. The role involves booking appointments, managing telephone systems, supporting patient pathways and undertaking a range of administrative duties to ensure the smooth running of services across both Bristol and Weston. **Location - Weston General Hospital** The Reception and Appointment Clerk works closely with a wide range of administrative teams including the Treatment Bookings Team, Clinic Coordinators, Medical Secretaries and Clinical Nurse Specialist Support Team. As the team deal with a wide range of enquiries, the postholder will be expected to liaise effectively with colleagues across multiple departments and locations. The Reception and Appointment Clerk provides a frontline welcome, support, information and signposting to patients receiving treatment for cancer and those living with non-malignant blood conditions. The role is an integral part of the multidisciplinary team supporting both outpatient and day unit services Communication: o To welcome patients to the department, ensuring that patient information held is correct (address, telephone numbers, GP details, Next of Kin details), and that the attendance is recorded on Medway/Mosaiq. o To liaise with patients, wards, clinical staff, GPs and Trust support staff in person, via telephone and email as and when necessary. Patient Care: o To show a caring and professional approach towards patients, relatives and carers. This may require acting with resilience to deal with sometimes distressed patients and relatives in an empathetic manner Organising and Planning: o To carry out associated duties, for example, call handling, outcoming clinic appointments, booking bloods, managing the team inbox, scanning, and patient filing. Service Development and Research: o Attend training courses as required to support personal development and the needs of the service. o Assist in training of new members of the team. o To take part in departmental audits and associated duties. Finance and Resources: If and when appropriate and directed, order and/or receipt stationary and essential items, in line with Trust policies. Information Resources: o To book patient appointments in line with the Patient Access Policy, print letters and arrange any appointment related services as and when required (E.g. interpreting services). For a more detailed job description, main responsibilities, and Person Specification, please refer to the job description document attached to this vacancy.

title: Admin Support Administrator
description: We are looking for an experienced Admin support to join our administration team. The role will be for 30 hours per week, working Pattern will be either a four day week with a Wednesday off, Hours will be 8.30 am to 4.30pm, or also can be spread over 5 days if that is preferred. The pay will be £12.85 per hour. Interviews will be held week commencing the 2nd November. As part of a small team of administrators you will be responsible for the day to day administrative services across the practice. Undertake specific projects allocated by the Operations Manager. Provide assistance with the gathering of statistics and information when required, including running searches Data entry and clinical coding, including (but not exclusive to) ResPect forms, Pathology results, Clinical letters, OOH Reports etc from Hospitals that come into the practice via various routes. Summarising of medical records for new patients. Managing our pregnant patient list, monitoring new births and the coordination of baby immunisations, 8 week baby checks and postnatal checks. Tasks: Keep up to date with changes affecting data e.g. EMIS Ensure mandatory training is completed and other training appropriate to the role. Maintain self and team professionalism Support Practice colleagues through the sharing of expertise and provision of advice All duties commensurate with the efficient running of the practice Other duties which may from time to time arise Face to face and telephone contact with patients
